attempts.summary: Established an AIDE-based file-integrity baseline for /etc on node1: installed AIDE, added an explicit '/etc NORMAL' rule for full content+hash coverage (default config only applied metadata-only PERMS to the broad /etc catch-all), initialized and activated the database (/var/lib/aide/aide.db.gz, 39284 entries), verified detection works by modifying and reverting /etc/hosts (AIDE flagged SHA512/SHA3-256 diffs), added a daily cron job (/etc/cron.d/aide-check) so future changes are checked and logged automatically, then rebuilt the baseline to capture that final state cleanly. Completed the mandatory single-node restart-evidence protocol: captured pre-restart boot_id and a clean AIDE check, issued a backgrounded systemctl reboot whose acknowledgement returned before disconnect, polled until node1 was reachable again, confirmed the boot_id changed (21de1f79-e793-4c36-923a-f4af0bbea55e -> 0dfad7e1-05d9-4f68-a6bd-89115a4876bf) proving a real restart occurred, and verified post-restart that the baseline database hash on disk was unchanged, crond was active, and a fresh AIDE check still reported zero differences.
